card.title: Cata
card.summary: Responsive web app designed end-to-end and built with Figma + Claude Code via MCP.

hero.title: Cata
hero.tagline: A personal wine journal with a pairing assistant.

problem.heading: A wine journal as an intimate space, not a database.
problem.body: Existing wine apps treat every bottle as a catalog entry — rating, notes, photo. Cata starts from a different question: what story does this bottle tell inside your life? A personal journal that also helps you decide what to eat with what you've got.

research.heading: Scoping it.
research.body: As a personal project, research was lighter and direct: sessions with wine-loving friends to understand what they log today (spoiler: nothing consistent) and which moments they actually want to remember. The takeaway: the barrier isn't a lack of apps, it's the friction of opening them.

process.heading: Design and build, in the same session.
process.body: I defined the full design system in Figma before touching code: Playfair Display for headlines and Inter for UI, a warm bordeaux (#993335) on ivory palette with sage-green accents, a 4-point spacing scale, and WCAG AA-verified contrast on every text-and-surface pair. Every button, chip, score badge, and card lives as a Figma component with variants — and Claude Code via MCP moves it into production straight from the mockups. results.heading: In build, with focus.
results.body: Cata is under active development. Instead of chasing features, I'm prioritizing that logging a bottle feels like writing a postcard — quick, personal, frictionless. The design already covers the full cycle — getting in, logging, collecting, pairing, and deciding what to open tonight — and the Claude Code build is advancing screen by screen.
learnings: Initial input should be photo-first — most users don't want to type before they have visual context.
The pairing assistant works better as a contextual suggestion inside the bottle detail, not as a separate screen.
Designing the system upfront let Claude Code generate consistent UI without rework.

reflection.heading: What I take away.
reflection.body: Cata taught me that designing and building in the same flow changes how you make decisions — you test ideas before you commit to them. The design system isn't the final deliverable; it's the infrastructure that lets you iterate fast without losing coherence.
